sections.title: 0 · Set the datum
sections.intro: Everything else is measured from two named faces, so name them once, here. From page 2 of the manual: the POWER barrel jack and the OUTPUT jack share one long side; INPUT and MIDI share the other. Those are the only fixed names I will use.

metrics.label: Which long side has POWER + OUTPUT?
metrics.how: Run your finger along each long side. One has a 9 V barrel jack and a 1/4" output; the other has a 1/4" input and a 5-pin MIDI. Record which is which as seen when the footswitch is nearest you.
metrics.hint: e.g. 'POWER/OUTPUT on my left, INPUT/MIDI on my right'

metrics.label: Which end has the footswitch and its LED?
metrics.how: That end is the toe end throughout this sheet. The treadle tips down toward it, and its pivot is at the far end.

metrics.label: Call the two ends
metrics.how: Confirm: toe end = footswitch end, hinge end = the opposite one, where the treadle's pivot bracket is visible.

sections.title: 1 · The body box
sections.intro: The outer shell below the top plate. Measure across the walls, not across the top plate - the top plate overhangs and will give you a bigger number. Take each reading twice, at two different places along the side, and put the worst pair in the note if they disagree.

metrics.label: Body width across (X), just above the feet
metrics.how: Calipers across the body at about 10 mm up from the bottom, jaws square to the walls. This is the widest point of the lower shell.

metrics.label: Body depth along (Y), just above the feet
metrics.how: Same height, but jaws on the two end walls.

metrics.label: Body width (X) just under the top plate
metrics.how: Repeat A1 as high as you can get the jaws, immediately below where the top plate starts. If this differs from A1, the walls are tapered and I need both.

metrics.label: Body depth (Y) just under the top plate
metrics.how: Repeat A2 as high as possible.

metrics.label: Body height: bottom face to the top plate's flat rim
metrics.how: Depth rod of the calipers from the bottom face (not the rubber feet) up to the flat rim of the top plate, at mid-length on a long side.

metrics.label: Highest point of the top plate
metrics.how: If the top plate is not flat - a raised area over the button panel, a lip, a boss - give the bottom face to that highest point.
metrics.hint: say 'flat' if A5 already is the highest

metrics.label: Body corner radius
metrics.how: Optional. Lay the calipers across a corner and read the widest gap, or just photograph one corner square-on with a ruler in frame and I will scale it.

image.caption: Side P elevation, from the manual's Page 2.

sections.title: 2 · The top plate and its overhang
sections.intro: The top plate overhangs the body on all four sides. Those overhangs are what a wall would have to tuck under, so they need to be real numbers rather than 'looks like a few mm'.

metrics.label: Top plate overhang, side P
metrics.how: Calipers across the top plate's edge and the body wall directly below it. Jaws horizontal, measuring how far the plate sticks out.

metrics.label: Top plate overhang, side I
metrics.how: Same on the other long side.

metrics.label: Top plate overhang, toe end
metrics.how: Same, but on the footswitch end.

metrics.label: Top plate overhang, hinge end
metrics.how: Same, on the opposite end.

metrics.label: Top plate thickness at its free edge
metrics.how: The plate's own edge thickness, measured on the overhanging brim.

metrics.label: Depth of the recess under the top plate
metrics.how: Under the overhanging brim, from the plate's underside down to the first thing below it - the body shoulder or the jack panel. This is the space an end wall would have to fit into.

image.caption: Side I elevation: note the top plate's lip and the recess beneath it.

sections.title: 3 · The five top-plate screws
sections.intro: These are the only fasteners on the pedal, and the whole mount hangs off them, so this section matters more than its length suggests. Photograph one head square-on with calipers on it, as well as filling in the numbers.

metrics.label: Number of these screws
metrics.how: Count them. They are black hex-socket heads flush-ish with the top plate.

metrics.label: Head across the flats
metrics.how: Jaws on two opposite flats of the hexagon, not on the corners.

metrics.label: Head across the corners
metrics.how: Jaws on two opposite corners - if it reads the same as C2 the head is round; if it reads bigger, it is a hex.

metrics.label: Head height above the plate
metrics.how: Depth rod, or the calipers' depth blade, from the plate's top face to the head's top face.

metrics.label: Hex key that fits the socket
metrics.how: Try your hex keys. Tell me the size that fits snugly.

metrics.label: Is the head sunk into a counterbore?
metrics.how: If the head sits in a recess, the plate's top face will be above the head.
metrics.hint: if yes, give the recess depth in the note

metrics.label: Thread major diameter (remove one screw)
metrics.how: Wind one out and put the calipers on the thread's outside. This tells me M3 vs M2.5, which decides every screw in the mount.

metrics.label: Screw length under the head
metrics.how: Same screw, from under the head to the tip.

metrics.label: Screw A position (side P at the toe end)
metrics.how: Lay the pedal flat, toe end toward you, side P on your left. With the calipers' depth rod, measure the screw centre from the side P wall and from the toe end wall, and give me both, 'x, y'.
metrics.hint: x from side-P wall, y from toe end

metrics.label: Screw B position (side P at the hinge end)
metrics.how: Same two references.

metrics.label: Screw C position (side I at the hinge end)
metrics.how: Same two references, but x is measured from the side I wall.

metrics.label: Screw D position (side I at the toe end)
metrics.how: Same.

metrics.label: Screw E position (any fifth screw)
metrics.how: Only if you counted 5 in C1 - the one that is not the four corners.

image.caption: Plan view. The small hexagon-headed features at the corners are these screws.

sections.title: 4 · The treadle — the section that decides the design
sections.intro: This is the part I got wrong last time, so it is worth slowing down here. I need the plate's true outline, where it sits relative to the body walls, and where it goes when you press it. Two photos taken square-on will help as much as the numbers: one at rest, one at full press, both with the calipers or a steel rule lying on the top plate.

metrics.label: Treadle plate width (X)
metrics.how: The metal plate's own width, widest point. Do not include the rubber tread pad if it overhangs; give both if it does.

metrics.label: Treadle plate length (Y)
metrics.how: Along the direction of travel.

metrics.label: Treadle plate thickness
metrics.how: Calipers on the plate's side edge where you can reach it - at the toe end, just above the rubber bumper.

metrics.label: Gap: treadle edge to side P wall
metrics.how: The clear gap between the treadle's edge and the inside of the body wall on side P, measured at the toe end.

metrics.label: Gap: treadle edge to side I wall
metrics.how: Same on side I. If T4 and T5 differ, the treadle is off-centre - I need both.

metrics.label: Gap: treadle toe to the toe end
metrics.how: From the plate's toe edge to the inside of the body's end wall.

metrics.label: Gap: treadle heel to the hinge end
metrics.how: From the plate's hinge-end edge to the body's end wall on that side. Usually hidden by the hinge bracket - get as close as you can and say so.

metrics.label: Treadle top height above the top-plate rim, at rest
metrics.how: Depth rod from the top plate's flat rim up to the treadle's top face, near the toe end.

metrics.label: Treadle top height above the rim at full press
metrics.how: Press the treadle all the way down and hold it, then repeat T8 at the same point. It should be lower - possibly below the rim.
metrics.hint: negative if it goes below the rim

metrics.label: Does the treadle dip below the top-plate rim at full press?
metrics.how: Say yes or no, and by how much if yes. This decides whether anything can sit over the top face at all on that side.

metrics.label: Hinge axis distance from the hinge end
metrics.how: The pivot's centre, from the body's end wall. Look for the bracket or the axle boss.

metrics.label: Hinge axis height above the bottom face
metrics.how: The pivot's centre height. Approximate is fine.

metrics.label: Rubber tread pad thickness
metrics.how: If the treadle has a glued rubber pad on top, its thickness, and whether it overhangs the metal plate.

image.caption: The treadle sits on its hinge bracket; the rubber bumper is under its free end.

sections.title: 5 · The four jacks
sections.intro: Positions along each long side, and how far the hardware sticks out. Heights are from the bottom face. If a jack's centre is hard to judge, measure to the edge of its nut and say so - I can work from that.

metrics.label: INPUT: distance from the toe end to its centre
metrics.how: Along side I.

metrics.label: INPUT: centre height above the bottom face
metrics.how: Vertical height of the jack's centreline.

metrics.label: MIDI: distance from the toe end to its centre
metrics.how: Along side I.

metrics.label: MIDI: centre height above the bottom face
metrics.how: Vertical.

metrics.label: OUTPUT: distance from the toe end to its centre
metrics.how: Along side P.

metrics.label: OUTPUT: centre height above the bottom face
metrics.how: Vertical.

metrics.label: POWER: distance from the toe end to its centre
metrics.how: Along side P. Measure to the barrel socket's centre, not the wall wart's box.

metrics.label: POWER: centre height above the bottom face
metrics.how: Vertical.

metrics.label: How far the 1/4" jack nuts stand proud of the wall
metrics.how: From the side wall's face out to the nut's outer face. One number is enough if all four match.

metrics.label: How far the POWER barrel stands out
metrics.how: Barrel jacks often protrude more than the 1/4" ones.

image.caption: POWER (barrel) and OUTPUT (1/4") on side P. INPUT and MIDI are the mirror image on side I.

sections.title: 6 · The feet, and the bottom face
sections.intro: The feet stay on the pedal - nothing gets removed - so the mount has to work around them. These four numbers set how the pedal sits on a plate.

metrics.label: Foot pad diameter
metrics.how: Across one rubber pad.

metrics.label: Foot pad height
metrics.how: How far the pad stands proud of the bottom face.

metrics.label: Foot pattern
metrics.how: Are there four, one near each corner, or two rails, or something else? Say which, and give one pad's centre as 'x from side-P wall, y from toe end'.

metrics.label: Is the bottom face flat and clear?
metrics.how: Any screws, plugs, ribs, or a recess. This is the one face the pedal rests on, so I need to know if it is interrupted.

sections.title: 7 · Where it sits on the board
sections.intro: Two questions about the RockBoard, so the QuickMount clips land on ribs rather than in slots. Look at the board with the pedal off it.

metrics.label: At the pedal's corner of the board, does the field start with a rib or a slot?
metrics.how: At the board's edge nearest where the pedal goes, look at the strip that runs along the edge: is the first thing a raised rib or an open slot?

metrics.label: Which corner of the board does the pedal sit in?
metrics.how: As you face the board, e.g. 'front right'.
